previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for persistent right shoulder pain following treatment for group B strep sepsis and polyarticular septic arthritis. Imaging revealed a lucency in the right humeral head suggestive of osteomyelitis. He underwent an incision and drainage procedure on 2174-07-31 under general anesthesia, tolerated it well, and had an uncomplicated postoperative course. Pain was managed with a transition from PCA to oral narcotics, and he was cleared for discharge to extended care on postoperative day one. He continues on clindamycin for infection, with instructions to perform pendulum exercises, keep the wound dry, and monitor for signs of complications. His cirrhosis and ascites were noted but stable during admission.

Brief Hospital Course:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:  ___ presenting with right sided abdominal 
pain, CT evidence of CBD dilation, and LFT's consistent with 
bile obstruction most consistent with acute choledocholithiasis.
.  
#.  Dilated CBD: Surgery consulted in the ED and recommended 
ERCP with papillotomy which would be diagnostic as well as 
therapeutic.  Patient put on empiric ciprofloxacin and flagy and 
made NPO except medications for surgery on hospital day Pain 
managed with IV dilaudid. ERCP preformed without complication.  
Patient brought back to floor with much improved pain and no new 
complaints.  Patient was advanced to tolerating clears post op 
and advanced to regular diet.  No overt GI bleeding seen.  2 d 
post procedure pt. felt at baseline.  His WBC were down however, 
a frequent occurence in him with acute 
illnesses/hospitalization, abx exposure.  After discussion with 
ERCP team, antibiotics (cipro/flagyl) were felt uneccessary, so 
were stopped.  He was instructed to continue his bactrim, 
however, per ID recommendation for ongoing ppx and treatement of 
his recent septic joints.  He will see his pcp in one week to 
have his cell counts checked.
.

___.  Signs and symptoms of chronic liver disease 
include jaundice, mild confusion, and fatigue.  He was continued

.  Continued on Bactrim DS 800mg-160mg 1 Tab PO qdaily per

Discharge Instructions:

to be secondary to a stone obstructing your bile duct.  You were 
put on IV antibiotics to prevent an infection and stabilized for

radiology_notes.text:
EXAM:  PA and lateral chest ___.

INDICATION:  Severe abdominal pain.

CHEST, TWO VIEWS:  Comparison made to ___.  Heart size remains normal. 
Mediastinal and hilar contours are normal.  The lungs are clear.  Bilateral
calcified hilar granulomas are unchanged.  There is no sign of free
intraperitoneal air.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process.

HISTORY:  ___ man with acute onset of severe abdominal pain.  Please
evaluate for mesenteric ischemia.  Patient has known hepatic cirrhosis.

TECHNIQUE:  CTA abdomen with and without contrast, and 3D reconstructions.  No
oral contrast administrated.

COMPARISON:  Compared to abdominal ultrasound ___.

FINDINGS:

LUNG BASES:  No pleural effusion, pulmonary nodule or opacity is seen in the
lung bases.

CT ABDOMEN:  The liver is small and coarse, consistent with a clinical
diagnosis of cirrhosis.  There is no definite focal hepatic lesion.  The
gallbladder is distended.  There is extra- and intra-hepatic bile duct
dilatation, common bile duct measuring 8 mm, findings which could suggest
recent passing of a gallstone, or abnormality at the ampulla. There is no
definite radiopaque gallstone seen. There is fat stranding around the
duodenum, gallbladder, and pancreatic head. Findings should be correlated with
the laboratory tests, and for clinical evidence of questionable acute
cholecystitis, or bile duct obstruction.

The main portal vein is patent.  IVC is patent.

The spleen is enlarged measuring 16 cm in largest diameter, with focal
calcification likely from prior granulomatous disease.  There are multiple
collaterals between the portal and systemic circulation, likely consistent
with the patient's known diagnosis of cirrhosis.  There is fat stranding
around the pancreatic head.

There is no evidence of mesenteric ischemia.  The abdominal vessels are
patent.  There is no evidence of small-bowel obstruction. There is normal
appearance of the loops of small and large bowel, keeping in consideration
lack of oral contrast.  Kidneys enhance symmetrically.  There is no evidence
of hydronephrosis.  There is no evidence of large focal masses in the kidneys.
The adrenal glands are unremarkable.

There is no evidence of significant lymphadenopathy in the mesenterium or
retroperitoneum; however, there are some scattered mesenteric lymph nodes,
which do not meet the CT criteria for pathologic enlargement.  There is no
evidence of acute appendicitis.  There is some small amount of free fluid in
the abdomen. There is no evidence of free air in the abdomen.

CT PELVIS:  The visualized loops of small bowel, large bowel, sigmoid appear
within normal limits with some limitation due to lack of administration of
oral contrast.  There is a small amount of free fluid in the pelvis.  The
bladder appears unremarkable.  The prostate and seminal vesicles appear
normal.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There are no suspicious lytic or sclerotic lesions in the
bones.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Intra- and extra-hepatic bile ducts dilatation.  Distended gallbladder.
Fat stranding around the gallbladder, duodenum and pancreatic head. Ascites.
Please correlate clinically for questionable bile duct obstruction,
cholecystitis, and with lab tests for pancreatatis. Findings were discussed
with Dr. ___ at 11:30 a.m, and posted on the ED dashboard.

2.  No evidence of small-bowel obstruction, or mesenteric ischemia.

3.  Portosystemic collaterals, and coarse and small liver with enlarged
spleen, findings consistent with known diagnosis of liver cirrhosis.

ERCP

COMPARISON:  None.

HISTORY:  Abdominal pain and abnormal LFTs and jaundice.

FINDINGS:  Seventeen fluoroscopic images were submitted for review without a
radiologist present.  These demonstrate mild proximal dilatation of the common
bile duct.  Per report, a common bile duct stone was extracted.  The
intrahepatic biliary tree was normal in appearance.

IMPRESSION:  Mild post-obstructive common bile duct dilatation. Extraction of
common bile duct stone per report.

Please see ERCP report for further details.
